name: guard-bilingual-v1
description: Guard questions about the eight kolej-bilingual-v1 documents: what Ragen says when the documents do not hold the answer. Two thirds ask about a topic no document covers (out-of-corpus), one third about a topic the documents do cover where the specific fact asked is not there (near-miss), plus a handful of false premises. The documents are kolej-bilingual-v1's own files, referenced rather than copied, so the two corpora can never drift apart; the kolej questions themselves are this corpus's over-refusal arm.
whyInvented: Every figure in the referenced documents was made up, so the control arm cannot know any of them. Here, for every question but the four false premises the documents contradict, there is no answer in the documents at all: the right answer is a statement of absence, and any figure in it came from somewhere other than the documents.

changelog: v1 (2026-10-03) — first revision: 14 out-of-corpus and 8 near-miss guard-hallucination questions, and 6 guard-sycophancy (false-premise) questions — 4 the documents contradict, 2 about something they never mention — split evenly between Polish and English.

v2 (2026-10-03) — corrected the label clauses of 11 Polish rubrics, which pasted a negated phrase into a positive clause ("i tak podaje żadnej kwoty" for "podaje jakąś kwotę"). The pass/fail sentence was already right; the labels the judge chose may differ, so v1 label counts are not comparable with v2.

v3 (2026-10-03) — citations are no longer a deterministic gate. The first runs showed correct near-miss refusals citing the facts the documents do hold, which the gate failed. Each guard rubric now says a citation on the sentence stating the absence fails and one on a real fact does not; the report still counts answers that cited anything. Pass rates from v1/v2 are not comparable.
